description: On a runner with Docker and systemd, against a test registry (the one from Host Maintenance's test, over HTTPS with a test CA) on ports 5055 and 4290. Two containers, one from each, are current; the second run is served from the cache, a root-only directory and file in the version 2 format. The state directory: a pre-made symlink is not followed and one not owned by root is not used (the check runs without saved state and says why); a symlink at the cache file is not read and is replaced, its target untouched. usrExcludePattern starting with - is a pattern. Rate limits: an error that only contains 4290 (the registry on that port stopped) is an unreadable image, not a rate limit, and the other image is still queried; a real 429 Too Many Requests trips the breaker. Staleness: a ref with no registry answer for 8 days alerts, naming it, the error kind (rate limited; refused) and since when; 2 days does not; usrStaleAfterDays 0 never does; a success clears it. Version 1 cache lines are read; malformed ones dropped. Every invalid input is refused, naming the variable. The input variables are read by their usr names; a variable set only under its old name (before version 3) is read from that, and when both are set the usr name wins. The container list is three docker commands (counted with a recording shim), retried when a container goes between docker ps and docker inspect, an error after three failed tries; a name holding a newline and tabs adds no row. A container run by image id is checked under its image's tag; one from an untagged image is skipped. A docker shim that never answers gives 'Docker did not answer within 40 seconds', exit 1, inside 90 seconds, nothing left running; TERM mid-run prints the fallback result block. docker.service stopped with docker.socket listening: exit 0, no docker command run, Docker still stopped. No docker command but a socket: exit 1; a client only in /snap/bin is found. GNU bash 4.2 runs the main paths. The first step reads the script itself: its time-limit functions sit in one block marked tc-docker bounded (a block CI compares with the other Docker monitors' copies), and its tc-docker running block says it is identical in every tc-docker component. Version 5: the result code is one block marked tc-docker result, shared with the other two Docker monitors (a step reads the script for it). A status of over 400 characters is printed whole (the limit is 900; it was 400). The directory an inherited TMP names is left alone on an early exit (the EXIT trap used to remove it), and the monitor's own scratch directory is gone after a full run and after TERM. A run with one unreadable image exits 0 and prints no diagnostic block.

set -e

cat > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-registry <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# tc-test-registry PORT DIR [CERT KEY]: a minimal image registry (the Docker
# Registry HTTP API v2, enough for docker push, docker pull and a manifest
# lookup) on 127.0.0.1, so a test can give an image a real registry digest
# without the internet. With CERT and KEY it serves HTTPS. Files in DIR change
# how it answers, so a test can switch them on and off:
#   htpasswd   "user:password": every request needs that Basic login
#   ratelimit  manifest requests get 429 Too Many Requests, as Docker Hub's do
#   delay      manifest requests wait this many seconds first
# Every manifest request is appended to DIR/requests.log.
import base64, hashlib, os, ssl, sys, time, uuid
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs
PORT, DIR = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
for sub in ("blobs", "uploads", "manifests"):
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(DIR, sub), exist_ok=True)
def safe(s): return s.replace("/", "_").replace(":", "_")
def sha(b): return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
def flag(n):
    try: return open(os.path.join(DIR, n)).read().strip()
    except OSError: return None
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def send(self, code, body=b"", headers=None):
        self.send_response(code)
        for k, v in (headers or {}).items(): self.send_header(k, v)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.send_header("Docker-Distribution-API-Version", "registry/2.0")
        self.end_headers()
        if self.command != "HEAD": self.wfile.write(body)
    def body(self):
        n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
        if n: return self.rfile.read(n)
        if self.headers.get("Transfer-Encoding", "").lower() != "chunked": return b""
        out = b""
        while True:
            size = int(self.rfile.readline().strip().split(b";")[0], 16)
            if size == 0: self.rfile.readline(); return out
            out += self.rfile.read(size); self.rfile.readline()
    def route(self):
        u = urlparse(self.path); p = u.path; q = parse_qs(u.query)
        login = flag("htpasswd")
        if login:
            want = "Basic " + base64.b64encode(login.encode()).decode()
            if self.headers.get("Authorization") != want:
                self.body()
                return self.send(401, b'{"errors":[{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"authentication required"}]}',
                                 {"WWW-Authenticate": 'Basic realm="tc-test-registry"', "Content-Type": "application/json"})
        if p in ("/v2", "/v2/"): return self.send(200, b"{}")
        if "/blobs/uploads/" in p:
            name, rest = p[4:].split("/blobs/uploads/", 1)
            if self.command == "POST":
                uid = uuid.uuid4().hex
                open(f"{DIR}/uploads/{uid}", "wb").close()
                return self.send(202, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/blobs/uploads/{uid}", "Range": "0-0", "Docker-Upload-UUID": uid})
            uid = rest.strip("/"); f = f"{DIR}/uploads/{uid}"
            with open(f, "ab") as fh: fh.write(self.body())
            if self.command == "PATCH":
                return self.send(202, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/blobs/uploads/{uid}", "Range": f"0-{max(os.path.getsize(f) - 1, 0)}", "Docker-Upload-UUID": uid})
            d = q["digest"][0]
            if sha(open(f, "rb").read()) != d: return self.send(400, b'{"errors":[{"code":"DIGEST_INVALID"}]}')
            os.replace(f, f"{DIR}/blobs/{safe(d)}")
            return self.send(201, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/blobs/{d}", "Docker-Content-Digest": d})
        if "/blobs/" in p:
            d = p.rsplit("/blobs/", 1)[1]; f = f"{DIR}/blobs/{safe(d)}"
            if not os.path.exists(f): return self.send(404, b'{"errors":[{"code":"BLOB_UNKNOWN"}]}')
            return self.send(200, open(f, "rb").read(), {"Docker-Content-Digest": d, "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream"})
        if "/manifests/" in p:
            name, ref = p[4:].rsplit("/manifests/", 1)
            if self.command == "PUT":
                data = self.body(); d = sha(data)
                for r in (ref, d):
                    open(f"{DIR}/manifests/{safe(name)}@{safe(r)}", "wb").write(data)
                    open(f"{DIR}/manifests/{safe(name)}@{safe(r)}.type", "w").write(self.headers.get("Content-Type", ""))
                return self.send(201, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/manifests/{d}", "Docker-Content-Digest": d})
            with open(f"{DIR}/requests.log", "a") as log: log.write(f"{self.command} {p}\n")
            delay = flag("delay")
            if delay: time.sleep(int(delay))
            if flag("ratelimit") is not None:
                return self.send(429, b'{"errors":[{"code":"TOOMANYREQUESTS","message":"You have reached your pull rate limit."}]}', {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
            f = f"{DIR}/manifests/{safe(name)}@{safe(ref)}"
            if not os.path.exists(f): return self.send(404, b'{"errors":[{"code":"MANIFEST_UNKNOWN","message":"manifest unknown"}]}', {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
            data = open(f, "rb").read()
            return self.send(200, data, {"Docker-Content-Digest": sha(data), "Content-Type": open(f + ".type").read()})
        return self.send(404)
    do_GET = do_HEAD = do_POST = do_PATCH = do_PUT = route
srv = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), H)
if len(sys.argv) > 4:
    ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER); ctx.load_cert_chain(sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4])
    srv.socket = ctx.wrap_socket(srv.socket, server_side=True)
srv.serve_forever()
EOF
cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-run <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-run [--bash42] [VAR=value...]: run the monitor as the harness does (a clean
# environment and the agent's root PATH); print its output, exit code and seconds taken.
b=/bin/bash; if [ "${1:-}" = --bash42 ]; then b=/opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash; shift; fi
t0=$(date +%s)
env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin HOME=/root "$@" "$b" "@MONITOR@"
rc=$?
secs=$(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))
echo "exit $rc after $secs seconds, under $("$b" -c 'echo "bash $BASH_VERSION"')"
[ "$secs" -lt 90 ] && echo "result inside 90 seconds"
exit 0
EOF

#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-state: the state directory and the cache file, or that they are not there.
d=/var/lib/tc-docker-monitor; f=$d/image-digests.tsv
ls -lad "$d" 2>&1

cat > /usr/local/bin/tc-test-reg <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-reg start|stop PORT: a test registry at https://tc-registry.test:PORT, its
# files (and switches: ratelimit, htpasswd, delay) in /tmp/tc-test-registry-PORT.
# tc-test-reg image NAME PORT: build a tiny image (sleep only), push it to that
# registry as tc-registry.test:PORT/tc-test-NAME:1 and print the digest.
# tc-test-reg run NAME PORT: run a container tc-NAME from that image.
D=/tmp/tc-test-registry-$3; [ "$1" = start ] || [ "$1" = stop ] && D=/tmp/tc-test-registry-$2
case "$1" in
start)
    mkdir -p "$D"; [ -s "$D.pid" ] && kill "$(cat "$D.pid")" 2>/dev/null; sleep 1
    setsid nohup python3 /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-registry "$2" "$D" /etc/tc-test-pki/registry.crt /etc/tc-test-pki/registry.key >"$D.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
    echo $! > "$D.pid"
    for i in $(seq 20); do curl -fsS "https://tc-registry.test:$2/v2/" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
    curl -fsS "https://tc-registry.test:$2/v2/" >/dev/null && echo "test registry answers on https://tc-registry.test:$2" ;;
stop)
    [ -s "$D.pid" ] && kill "$(cat "$D.pid")" 2>/dev/null; rm -f "$D.pid"; sleep 1
    curl -fsS "https://tc-registry.test:$2/v2/" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "test registry STILL ANSWERS" || echo "test registry on $2 stopped" ;;
image)
    r=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$r/bin"; cp /bin/sleep "$r/bin/"
    for l in $(ldd /bin/sleep | grep -oE '/[^ ]+'); do mkdir -p "$r$(dirname "$l")"; cp "$l" "$r$l"; done
    ref="tc-registry.test:$3/tc-test-$2:1"
    tar -C "$r" -c . | docker import --change "LABEL tc.nonce=$(date +%s%N)" --change 'CMD ["/bin/sleep","86400"]' - "$ref" >/dev/null
    rm -rf "$r"
    docker push -q "$ref" >/dev/null || echo "PUSH FAILED: $ref"
    docker image inspect -f "$ref {{json .RepoDigests}}" "$ref" ;;
run)
    docker rm -f "tc-$2" >/dev/null 2>&1
    docker run -d --name "tc-$2" "tc-registry.test:$3/tc-test-$2:1" >/dev/null && echo "running tc-$2" ;;
esac
EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-registry /usr/local/bin/tc-test-run /usr/local/bin/tc-test-left /usr/local/bin/tc-test-dstate /usr/local/bin/tc-test-state /usr/local/bin/tc-test-reg
mkdir -p /etc/tc-test-pki; cd /etc/tc-test-pki
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 2 -subj /CN=tc-test-ca -keyout ca.key -out ca.crt -addext basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE -addext keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign 2>/dev/null
openssl req -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -subj /CN=tc-registry.test -keyout registry.key -out registry.csr 2>/dev/null
printf 'subjectAltName=DNS:tc-registry.test\nbasicConstraints=CA:FALSE\nextendedKeyUsage=serverAuth\n' > ext
openssl x509 -req -in registry.csr -CA ca.crt -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial -days 2 -out registry.crt -extfile ext 2>/dev/null
grep -q ' tc-registry.test$' /etc/hosts || echo '127.0.0.1 tc-registry.test' >> /etc/hosts
for p in 5055 4290; do mkdir -p /etc/docker/certs.d/tc-registry.test:$p && cp ca.crt /etc/docker/certs.d/tc-registry.test:$p/ca.crt; done
cp ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/tc-test-ca.crt && update-ca-certificates >/dev/null 2>&1
cd /
docker rm -f $(docker ps -aq) >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
rm -rf /var/lib/tc-docker-monitor
tc-test-reg start 5055
tc-test-reg start 4290
tc-test-reg image cur 5055
tc-test-reg image other 4290

steps.label: bash 4.2: build GNU bash 4.2 from the GNU release (sha256 checked) into /opt/tc-bash42; it has the bug: an empty array is unbound under set -u
steps.run:
set -e
d=$(mktemp -d); cd "$d"
for u in https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/bash/bash-4.2.tar.gz https://ftpmirror.gnu.org/bash/bash-4.2.tar.gz; do
  curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o bash-4.2.tar.gz "$u" && break
done
echo 'a27a1179ec9c0830c65c6aa5d7dab60f7ce1a2a608618570f96bfa72e95ab3d8  bash-4.2.tar.gz' | sha256sum -c -
tar xzf bash-4.2.tar.gz
cd bash-4.2
# 2011 C: -std=gnu89 goes in CC so it also reaches the build-time tools (CC_FOR_BUILD), which a
# newer gcc defaulting to C23 otherwise refuses; the old-style warnings stay warnings.
W='-O1 -fpermissive -Wno-implicit-function-declaration -Wno-implicit-int -Wno-int-conversion -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types -Wno-return-mismatch'
gcc --version | head -n 1
CC='gcc -std=gnu89' CFLAGS="$W" CFLAGS_FOR_BUILD="$W" ./configure --without-bash-malloc --disable-nls >configure.log 2>&1 || { tail -n 30 configure.log; exit 1; }
make -j"$(nproc)" >make.log 2>&1 || { grep -m 20 'error:' make.log; tail -n 30 make.log; exit 1; }
install -D -m 755 bash /opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash
/opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash -c 'echo "built bash $BASH_VERSION"'
/opt/tc-bash42/bin/bash -c 'set -u; a=(); echo "${a[@]}"' 2>&1 || true

#!/bin/sh

    @REAL@ "$@"; rc=$?
    echo deaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddead
    exit $rc
fi
exec @REAL@ "$@"
EOF
